trial_court: CIVIL JUDGE-01 (SOUTH) SAKET COURT, NEW DELHI - CS SCJ 85068/16
case_name: ANKUSH GUPTA VS. BALJEET SINGH AND ANS.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: ANKUSH GUPTA, Prop. M/s Bath Interior and Decorators
parties.respondent_defendant: SH. BALJEET SINGH (Defendant No. 1) and I P INTERIORS (Defendant No. 2)

facts_of_case: The plaintiff is the proprietor of M/s Bath Interior and Decorators and runs a shop at D-86, Hauz Khas. The defendants persuaded the plaintiff to supply goods on credit basis, which was to be paid within few days after delivery. The plaintiff supplied goods worth Rs. 89,746/- and claims recovery of this amount along with pendente-lite and future interest.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his case.
legal_principles.held: It is stated that plaintiff has completely failed to show as to how the defendants are liable to pay a sum of Rs. 89,746/- to the plaintiff.

legal_principles.principle: A party's averments must be supported by evidence.
legal_principles.held: To prove his case, plaintiff himself stepped into the witness box as PW-1 and tendered his affidavit as Ex. PW1/A and placed reliance upon the following documents.

outcome.final_order: The suit is decreed for the recovery of Rs. 89,746/- alongwith pendente-lite and future interest @ 24% from the date of filing of the suit till the date of actual realization of the outstanding amount due and payable by the defendants to the plaintiff.
